verdicts.trueWording: The Chicago Manual of Style, 17th edition
verdicts.note: Raw PDF (curl, 402KB, application/pdf; pdftotext -layout, 11 pages). Opening section lists two primary resources -- Chicago 17th and Merriam-Webster's Collegiate 11th -- then says the guide takes both works as its foundation. Footer on all 11 pages reads Version 1.08a (c)2018 Wizards of the Coast. Quote appears word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: The Chicago Manual of Style, 16th edition
verdicts.note: Raw PDF (curl, 1.24MB; pdftotext -layout, 9 pages). Opening section of v1.04a lists Chicago 16th plus Merriam-Webster's Collegiate 11th, then: 'Because this guide takes both of those works as its foundation'. Footer reads Version 1.04a (c)2013. The comparative limb (one Chicago edition of movement) was confirmed against the v1.08a raw text fetched in the same run, which reads 17th; both endpoints measured, not inferred.

Raw PDF. The footer line occurs on all nine pages (extracted lines 54, 107, 160, 218, 282, 338, 397, 457, 514), matching the claim's 'running footer, every page'. Whitespace between the version and the copyright is column padding from -layout extraction, not extra words.

verdicts.trueWording: Pages carry only the corporate copyright footer; no personal name
verdicts.note: Both PDFs read raw end to end. Page counts match the source field exactly (v1.08a 11 pages, v1.04a 9 pages). No 'Credits', 'written by', 'compiled', or editor/author byline anywhere in either body text; a name-shaped scan (Mohan, Crawford, Perkins, Mearls, Wyatt, Schwalb, Cordell, Winter, Lysa) returned zero hits in both. Final pages are weapon/armor compound lists, not credits. CAVEAT the downstream document should carry: the v1.08a FILE metadata names Author 'Kim Mohan' (v1.04a metadata says 'Lysa'). That is document properties, not a page, so the claim as worded ('anywhere in its pages') stands -- but 'the only attribution is the corporate copyright line' is true of the printed pages only, not of the file.

verdicts.trueWording: neutrality by writing in the second person
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, 'Achieving Gender Neutrality' section: the guide prefers this in rules text 'whenever possible'. Quote is contiguous across a column line break in the original layout. The claim's 'wherever possible' is its own paraphrase of the page's 'whenever possible'; the quoted fragment itself matches word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: We avoid page references as much as possible.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, 'Page References' subsection under Cross-References. Sentence appears word for word as the section's opening line.

verdicts.trueWording: They are labor-intensive (they must be added by
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, 'Page References'. Full sentence continues 'hand during galley review), and they invite error.' Quote matches word for word and every limb (labor-intensive; added by hand; during galley review) is on the page. Flag for the downstream editor: the guide gives TWO reasons in that one sentence -- labor-intensiveness AND that page references invite error -- so the claim's definite 'The guide's stated reason' should not be read as the only reason.
Raw PDF, 'Cross-References' section. Next sentence supplies the claim's reason limb: they are useful tools that can be easily overused.

verdicts.trueWording: Set a monster’s name in bold only the first time
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, 'Terms to Set in Bold'. Sentence completes 'it appears in an encounter area or other subsection', supporting both the encounter-area/subsection limb and the not-every-mention limb. Apostrophe in the source is a typographic curly apostrophe.

verdicts.trueWording: Make sure no text gets between the number of
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, 'Terms to Set in Bold'. Sentence completes 'monsters appearing and the name of the stat block', with the worked example: write 'four goblins', not 'four loud goblins'. The page says 'no text', which covers the claim's narrower 'any word'.

verdicts.trueWording: The italicized terms are treated as titles
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, 'Terms to Italicize' (list covers artifacts, magic items, spells; continues onto the next page). Page continues: don't confuse one of these titles with an effect it creates, with the wall of fire spell example -- which supports the claim's 'rather than as descriptions of the thing they create' limb.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the appositive 'the Planescape line's editor' -- the page has Vallese saying he was hired as an editor and assigned to the Planescape line, and it explicitly names a co-equal: the other primary Planescape editor of that era was Michele Carter. The definite article asserting a sole line editor is not what the page supports.
verdicts.trueWording: written in a wry, overly clever voice that smirked
verdicts.note: Raw HTML fetched with a browser user agent (759KB, 200) and stripped to text. Quote is word for word in Ray's answer on Planescape's reputation. The page's object of the smirking is 'all the clueless bashers stumbling around the multiverse'; the claim's gloss 'the setting's ignorant outsiders' is a fair reading of Planescape cant and is NOT the reason for the PARTIAL. Repair is one word: 'a Planescape editor' rather than 'the Planescape line's editor'.

verdicts.trueWording: not people using slang he didn’t understand to discuss philosophy
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Monte's answer on the WotC purchase reads: WotC president Peter Adkison loved planar stuff, but he wanted guys hitting demons with swords, not people using slang he didn't understand to discuss philosophy and ethics. Speaker attribution (Monte), Adkison's title (WotC president) and the slang/philosophy limb are all on the page; the claim simply stops before 'and ethics'. Apostrophe in the source is curly.

Wayback raw PDF capture (3.8MB, application/pdf, 107 pages; pdftotext -layout). Sentence appears word for word in the December 2011 / DUNGEON 197 column running-headed 'The Dungeon Master Experience: T'wit', inside the list introduced by 'Here are a few specific tactics that I use'. The 'I' is Christopher Perkins: the compilation's front matter and its credits page both name him, and the column is his standing series.

verdicts.trueWording: I keep my NPC descriptions brief as well.
verdicts.note: Same raw Wayback PDF, same T'wit column, roughly nineteen extracted lines after the previous item and under the same 'tactics that I use' list. Sentence appears word for word; the Vantajar example that follows (one distinguishing characteristic, everything else left to the players' imaginations) supports the brevity limb.
